I was by the beach when it was overcast and stormy, and sometimes I would be sitting on the sands watching big waves come rolling to the shore, and other times I was driving a car in heavy traffic on a highway overlooking the sea. It was raining in this dream, and the beach was right next to the highway, and sometimes I could see myself on the sand and sometimes I could see myself in traffic. I heard blaring horns and angry people shouting, and the long line of cars that stretched far into the horizon never seemed to budge. This wasn't a pretty place. It was strewn with litter and up ahead in the distance I saw long highway bridges crossing the sea, and more ugly concrete structures washed in rain. But the roads looked shiny while I was in traffic, I could see the taillights reflected on the wet asphalt.

Then I remember sitting by what looked like a giant abandoned pool, like it was part of some giant plaza. The forest was all around me, and I think the sky was an ugly yellow tinted green, which I thought meant I was in South America or Cuba or some place tropical. The pool was a dark ugly green and I saw big strands of algae floating on the surface or reaching from the bottom like kelp. And I remember seeing myself fall in the pool, and I saw myself turn darker and murkier as I reached the bottom, and I leaped into the pool to save myself from drowning, but I'd grown small and when I threw myself over the pool's edge I was turned into a tiny shriveling infant with black beads for eyes. I didn't make any noises though. I looked at myself quite puzzled but not very scared at all.

Then I was in a library somewhere, and I wasn't alone this time, there were crowds of people but I couldn't see their faces. And a guy who looked like Joe Rogan walked up to me, and yeah until now everything sounded all meaningful and poetic or whatever, and said, "Where do I put the shelves?" And he wasn't holding the shelves or anything but I was sure he had some shelves on him, and I told him to put it there, of course. Was I a librarian? That would be cool. I think I was organizing a meeting for a bunch of Marxists at the library, and they'd bring a whole bunch of obscure leftist books and zines, and they'd all read it together. I hung up posters about socialism and signs advertising the meeting.

So the rest of the dream was me reading the books they brought. I read it in a nice room with bean bags for chairs. One book was red with bright letters called, "GRIND", like the daily grind, which is a lot more clever a title than my brain usually thinks of when I'm dreaming. And the other one looked old and worn and was apparently about a poor family living in the South, but when I opened the book up a video played, with voice narration and all, about an engineer who was also a chef. I can remember some of what this guy was saying, and it was pretty funny in retrospect:

"I made a special recipe, and some people asked me what it was, and they were surprised when I said it was deep fried penis wrapped in bacon," and I remember simply accepting this at face value. Okay, so he deep fried some penises. Now I'm thinking, "eww." What a waste of dick. I'm kind of jealous how my dream self can be so nonchalant of all the terrible and strange things happening, and I wish I had that kind of mental fortitude.

And then he said, while I saw him (in the book? My thoughts within the dream about the book? I don't know) wearing glasses and flipping some normal non-penis meats on a grill, "No one thinks I'm a chef, they think I'm just an engineer, they see me throwing butter on a grill, they think I'm making something." Very surreal stuff. I vaguely had the feeling that the penis chef was a modern-day descendant of the poor southern family, who was talking about his family's legacy, but other than that it made no sense.

The first part of the dream scared me, like I was looking into myself and seeing nothing, but the second part was funny in a strange way, probably just out of shock. I think this has been one of the nicer dreams I've had in awhile, all I've had before were nightmares and choking and being paralyzed and I think any sort of not-awful in a dream is a welcome relief.

Great, yet another post by someone who clearly doesn't know what he's talking about, making nonsense arguments.

Blockstream is a company, companies try to make money, therefor blockstream is bad. Sound logic...

86% of Linux is being developed by commercial companies, it's unrealistic to think this won't happen with bitcoin. Nor is it in any way realistic to expect these highly skilled developers to work for free.

It's not the "trying to make money is bad". The OP is pointing out that some core devs are in the position of conflicting interest: Core improvement vs side project profitability. It would be fine if blockstream was investing in bitcoin itself. But it's investing in a project that builds on top of bitcoin shortcomings.

It doesn't come across as such, but it's a good point to make.

It's stupid, but I never really realized people see this as projects on top of bitcoin and not as a part of bitcoin. I feel that a large part of that comes from the utopian believe bitcoin can scale by just increasing the blocksize, without massively centralizing it to the point it hurts. This is a scaling problem we don't have a solution for, so when someone proposes an idea that fixes this in a way that requires no fundamental trust in the sense that you can't lose your money I feel like it's a part of bitcoin.

What also is important to realize is that if we get lightning network wrong and it doesn't work in practice, for instance all LN-nodes will require KYC, we can consider it a failure and we can search for other ways to scale bitcoin. However, if we get the scaling by blocksize wrong, there's no turning back, there'll be no bitcoin as we know it.
Except we do have a working and running in the wild implementation of BIP101 and not even a final spec for Lightning nor sidechains.

That only becomes relevant if we get full blocks and it becomes too expensive without alternative solutions by january 2016.
Given the support BIP 100 gets I think there will be an alternative solution ready.

Great post, well said!

Blockstream has become a cancer to Bitcoin. There is so much conflict of interest there.

With any major corporation there are rules and regulations surrounding conflicts of interest. I think it's time Bitcoin adopted some of those. You can't seriously believe that Core developers who are getting paid by Blockstream, which will profit from smaller blocks, are not going to be influenced by that employment contract. Of course they are going to find reasons why the block size should be smaller, whether they are conscious of it or not. It's human nature.
